chunks: Zurarah asked Abā Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام about the time of the Dhuhr prayer, so he said:
"One cubit from the sun’s decline; and the time of ʿAsr is two cubits from the time of Dhuhr, so that is four feet from the sun’s decline."

Then he said: "The wall of the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was one stature high, and when one cubit of shadow had passed from it, he performed Dhuhr, and when two cubits had passed from it, he performed ʿAsr."

Then he said: "Do you know why one cubit and two cubits were set?" I said: "Why was that set?" He said: "Because of the nafilah prayer. You may perform nafilah from the sun’s decline until one cubit passes; then when your shadow reaches one cubit, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the nafilah. And when your shadow reaches two cubits, you begin with the obligatory prayer and leave the nafilah."

key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: supererogatory prayer performed before the obligatory prayer
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: a cubit, used here as a measure of shadow length
key_terms.ذِرَاعَانِ: two cubits, used here as a measure for the later prayer time
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the start of the prayer period
key_terms.فَيْئُكَ: your returning shade or shadow after the sun’s decline
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the time of the ʿAsr prayer
key_terms.وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the time of the Dhuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith define the times of Dhuhr and ʿAsr and the place of nafilah before them?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the timing of Dhuhr and ʿAsr in relation to the sun’s decline and the measured increase of shadow. It also clarifies that these measurements were set to provide room for the nafilah prayers before the obligatory salat. The report preserves the practice associated with the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as a practical standard for prayer times.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.653 – Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about the timing of the Dhuhr (noon) prayer.
Imam (as) replied: "It is one arm's length (shadow) from the sun's decline, and the time for Asr (afternoon) is two arm's lengths from the time of Dhuhr, which is four feet from the sun's decline."

He then added, "The wall of the Prophet’s Mosque (sw) was as high as a person's stature, and when a shadow reached one arm's length, the Dhuhr prayer would be performed, and when it reached two arm's lengths, the Asr prayer would be performed."

He then asked: "Do you know why the measure of one and two arm's lengths was set?"
I said: "Why was that made so?"
Imam (as) said: "It is for the sake of the supererogatory (nafilah) prayers. You may perform the supererogatory prayers from the sun's decline until the shadow reaches one arm's length; when it reaches one arm's length, you begin the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer. When it reaches two arm's lengths, you begin the obligatory prayer and leave the supererogatory prayer."
